translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang, and others entered in relief. In the seventh month the Nian rebels were pacified, and his palace rank and peacock feather were restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，回京，管理戶部三庫，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned to the capital, administered the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and was appointed imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned to the capital, administered the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and was appointed imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，優詔賜卹，贈太保，賜金治喪，遣惠郡王奠醊，祀賢良祠，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; a special edict granted mourning honors; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian; gold for funeral expenses was bestowed; Prince Hui was sent to pour the libation; he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies; and he was given the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died. A special edict granted mourning honors; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian; gold for funeral expenses was bestowed; Prince Hui was sent to pour the libation; he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies; and he was given the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 尋以疆臣請合祀湖北胡林翼專祠。

translations.literal: Soon, at the request of frontier officials, he was enshrined jointly in Hu Linyi's dedicated temple in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, at the request of frontier officials, he was enshrined jointly in Hu Linyi's dedicated temple in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 當官文之在湖北，事事聽林翼所為，惟馭下不嚴，用財不節，林翼憂之。

translations.literal: When Guan Wen was in Hubei, he let Hu Linyi do as he pleased in every matter; only in controlling subordinates he was not strict, and in spending money he was not frugal — Hu Linyi worried about this.
translations.idiomatic: While Guan Wen held Hubei, he deferred to Hu Linyi in every matter; yet he was lax with subordinates and extravagant with funds, and Hu Linyi worried about it.

sentences.zh: 閻敬銘方佐治餉，一日林翼與言，恐誤疆事。

translations.literal: Yan Jingming was then assisting in managing supplies; one day Hu Linyi spoke with him, fearing this might harm frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jingming was then helping manage supplies; one day Hu Linyi confided in him, fearing these failings might harm frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 敬銘曰：「公誤矣！

translations.literal: Jingming said: 「You are mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: Jingming said: 「You are mistaken!

sentences.zh: 本朝不輕以漢大臣專兵柄。

translations.literal: Our dynasty does not lightly entrust sole command of troops to Han Chinese grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty does not lightly give Han ministers sole command of armies.

sentences.zh: 今滿、漢並用，而聲績炳著者多屬漢人，此聖明大公劃除畛域之效。

translations.literal: Now Manchu and Han are employed together, yet those whose fame and achievement shine brightest are mostly Han — this is the effect of the sage emperor's great fairness in erasing boundary lines.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han serve side by side today, yet most of the men whose fame and deeds shine brightest are Han — proof of the emperor's sage fairness in breaking down old divisions.

sentences.zh: 然湖北居天下要衝，朝廷寧肯不以親信大臣臨之？

translations.literal: Yet Hubei occupies the empire's strategic crossroads — would the court really fail to place a trusted intimate minister over it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hubei sits at the empire's strategic crossroads — would the court really leave it without a trusted minister of its own?

sentences.zh: 夫督撫相劾，無論未必勝，即勝，能保後來者必賢耶？

translations.literal: If governor-general and governor impeach each other, leaving aside that victory is not assured — even if one wins, can one guarantee the successor will be worthy?
translations.idiomatic: If governor-general and governor turn on each other, victory is far from assured — and even if you win, who can guarantee the next man will be better?

sentences.zh: 且繼者或厲清操，勤庶務，而不明遠略，未必不顓己自是，豈甘事事讓人？

translations.literal: Moreover a successor may be strict in personal integrity and diligent in routine affairs yet lacking in far-reaching strategy — not necessarily free from insisting on his own judgment — would he willingly yield in every matter?
translations.idiomatic: A successor may be upright and diligent in routine business yet blind to the larger strategy — likely to insist on his own way. Would he willingly defer in everything?

sentences.zh: 官文心無成見，兼隸旗籍，每有大事，正可藉其言以伸所請。

translations.literal: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices, and he is moreover enrolled in the banner rolls — whenever there is a great matter, one can exactly borrow his voice to advance what one requests.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen has no fixed prejudices, and as a bannerman he can speak for you on great matters and carry your requests forward.

sentences.zh: 其失僅在私費奢豪，誠於事有濟，歲糜十萬金供之，未為失計。

translations.literal: His fault lies only in lavish private spending; if it truly helps affairs succeed, supplying him with a hundred thousand taels of gold each year would not be a bad plan.
translations.idiomatic: His fault is only private extravagance; if it keeps affairs running, a hundred thousand taels a year would not be money wasted.

sentences.zh: 至一二私人，可容，容之；

translations.literal: As for one or two personal favorites — if they can be tolerated, tolerate them;
translations.idiomatic: As for one or two personal favorites — tolerate them if you can;

sentences.zh: 不可，則以事劾去之。

translations.literal: if not, then impeach and remove them on grounds of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: if not, impeach them on specific grounds and have them removed.

sentences.zh: 彼意氣素平，必無忤也。

translations.literal: His temperament has always been even — he will certainly not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: His temper has always been even — he will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 」林翼大悟。

translations.literal: 」Hu Linyi was greatly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hu Linyi saw it clearly at once.

sentences.zh: 及林翼歿，督撫不相能，官文劾嚴樹森去之；

translations.literal: When Hu Linyi died, governor-general and governor could not work together; Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and had him removed;
translations.idiomatic: After Hu Linyi died, governor-general and governor fell out; Guan Wen impeached Yan Shusen and had him removed;

sentences.zh: 而曾國荃又劾官文去之。

translations.literal: and Zeng Guoquan in turn impeached Guan Wen and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: and Zeng Guoquan in turn impeached Guan Wen and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 官文晚節建樹不能如曩時，然林翼非官文之虛己推誠，亦無以成大功，世故兩賢之。

translations.literal: Guan Wen's achievements in his later years could not match earlier times; yet without Guan Wen's emptying himself and yielding in good faith, Hu Linyi would not have been able to complete the great achievement — hence the age esteems both as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen's achievements in his later years never matched his earlier record; yet without Guan Wen's self-effacing trust, Hu Linyi could not have finished the great work — and so the age honors both men.

sentences.zh: 孫興恩，襲伯爵。

translations.literal: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingen inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 文煜，字星岩，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Yu, styled Xingyan, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu, styled Xingyan, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 由官學生授太常寺庫使，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: From student of the Imperial School he was appointed storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted step by step to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a student of the Imperial School, he was appointed storekeeper of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and rose step by step to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸霸昌道、四川按察使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as intendant of Bazhang Circuit in Zhili and provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as intendant of Bazhang Circuit in Zhili and provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時江寧已陷賊，文煜從琦善江北大營。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangning had already fallen to the rebels; Wen Yu followed Qi Shan at the Great Camp north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning had already fallen to the rebels; Wen Yu followed Qi Shan at the Great Camp north of the river.

sentences.zh: 四年，琦善歿於揚州，所部練勇及江北糧台事宜，命文煜接辦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Qi Shan died at Yangzhou; the trained braves under his command and affairs of the grain depot north of the river were ordered transferred to Wen Yu to take over.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Qi Shan died at Yangzhou; Wen Yu was ordered to take over his trained braves and the grain depot north of the river.

sentences.zh: 五年春，粵匪由瓜洲東竄沙頭港，文煜遣勇擊之，賊由對岸扎簰爭渡，偕水師以大砲合擊，賊退瓜洲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the Guangdong rebels fled east from Guazhou into Shatou Port; Wen Yu sent braves to strike them; the rebels on the opposite bank rafted bamboo floats to force a crossing; together with the navy he opened fire with great guns in combined attack, and the rebels retreated to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year Guangdong rebels fled east from Guazhou toward Shatou Port. Wen Yu sent braves against them; the rebels rafted bamboo floats from the opposite bank to force a crossing, but he joined the navy in a barrage of great guns and drove them back to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 文煜以沙頭港為裡下河門戶，賊所必爭，築土城砲台，疏請添募練勇守禦，從之。

translations.literal: Wen Yu regarded Shatou Port as the gateway to the Inner Lower River — ground the rebels were sure to contest — and built earthen walls and gun platforms; he memorialized requesting additional recruitment of trained braves for defense; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu saw Shatou Port as the gateway to the Inner Lower River — ground the rebels were bound to fight for — and built earthen walls and gun platforms; he memorialized to recruit more trained braves for its defense, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 既而賊踞揚州，窺裡下河，文煜擊之於萬安橋，大有斬獲，賊勢乃挫。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels held Yangzhou and eyed the Inner Lower River; Wen Yu attacked them at Wan'an Bridge with heavy kills and captures, and rebel momentum was blunted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels held Yangzhou and eyed the Inner Lower River; Wen Yu struck them at Wan'an Bridge with heavy kills and captures, and their momentum broke.

sentences.zh: 七年，調江蘇布政使，治江南大營糧台。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangsu and managed the grain depot of the Great Camp south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangsu and took charge of the grain depot of the Great Camp south of the river.

sentences.zh: 以支給撙節，為軍中所不便，提督和春劾其拘泥，命來京候另簡用。

translations.literal: Because his disbursements were frugal — inconvenient for the army — Grand Coordinator He Chun impeached him for rigid adherence to rules; he was ordered to come to the capital awaiting another appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His frugal disbursements inconvenienced the army; Grand Coordinator He Chun impeached him for rigid adherence to rules, and he was ordered to the capital to await a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed financial commissioner of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed financial commissioner of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 九年，英兵犯大沽，為僧格林沁擊退。

translations.literal: In the ninth year English troops attacked Dagu and were driven back by Sengge Rinchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year English troops attacked Dagu and were driven back by Sengge Rinchen.

sentences.zh: 戰後將議撫，命文煜從總督恆福赴北塘相機辦理。

translations.literal: After the battle, when peace negotiations were about to be discussed, Wen Yu was ordered to follow Governor Hengfu to Beitang to handle matters as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle, as peace talks were about to begin, Wen Yu was ordered to follow Governor Hengfu to Beitang and handle matters as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 尋擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 捻匪圍曹縣，分黨擾安陵，檄曹州鎮總兵郝上庠合師內外夾擊，解曹州圍，安陵賊亦退。

translations.literal: Nian bandits besieged Cao County and divided into factions to harass Anling; he ordered Cao Prefecture Brigade Commander Hao Shangxiang to unite forces in pincer attack from within and without; the siege of Cao Prefecture was lifted, and the rebels at Anling also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bandits besieged Cao County and sent detachments to raid Anling; he ordered Cao Prefecture Brigade Commander Hao Shangxiang to unite forces in a pincer from within and without, lifted the siege of Cao Prefecture, and the rebels at Anling withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，捻匪又竄單縣，分擾嶧縣得勝徬，遣將擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Nian bandits again fled into Shan County and sent detachments to raid Yixian's Desheng Embankment; he dispatched generals to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Nian bandits again fled into Shan County and sent detachments to raid Desheng Embankment in Yixian; he dispatched generals and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 英法聯軍踞砲台，文煜遣兵扼利津，自駐濰縣韓亭以防陸路北犯。

translations.literal: The Anglo-French allied army held the forts; Wen Yu sent troops to block Lijin and personally garrisoned Hanting in Weixian to guard against a land invasion from the north.
translations.idiomatic: The Anglo-French allied army held the forts; Wen Yu sent troops to block Lijin and personally garrisoned Hanting in Weixian to guard against a land invasion from the north.

sentences.zh: 尋敵船北駛犯北塘，文煜分軍入衛，駐通州，自率眾赴濟寧剿捻匪。

translations.literal: Soon enemy ships sailed north and attacked Beitang; Wen Yu divided troops to enter the capital guard, garrisoned Tongzhou, and personally led a force to Jining to suppress Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemy ships sailed north and attacked Beitang; Wen Yu divided his forces to reinforce the capital guard and garrisoned Tongzhou, while he personally led troops to Jining to suppress Nian bandits.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署直隸總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he acted as governor-general of Zhili; soon he received full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he acted as governor-general of Zhili, and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 時和議既成，穆宗回鑾，畿輔馬賊四起，久未淨絕，屢詔責文煜搜捕。

translations.literal: At the time peace had been concluded and the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital; mounted bandits rose everywhere in the capital region and long went uncleaned out; edicts repeatedly blamed Wen Yu for failing to hunt them down.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had been concluded and the Muzong Emperor returned to the capital, yet mounted bandits rose everywhere in the capital region and long went uncleaned out; edicts repeatedly blamed Wen Yu for failing to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，坐山東降賊張錫珠等擾畿南督剿不力，褫職，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, on grounds that surrendered Shandong rebels Zhang Xizhu and others harassed the south of the capital region and he had been ineffective in supervising suppression, he was stripped of office and sent to garrison duty on the military frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, because surrendered Shandong rebels under Zhang Xizhu and others harassed the south of the capital region and he had failed to suppress them effectively, he was stripped of office and sent to garrison duty on the military frontier.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧格林沁奏調赴營差遣，尋授鑲黃旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year Sengge Rinchen memorialized to transfer him to camp service; soon he was appointed deputy commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Sengge Rinchen memorialized to transfer him to camp service, and soon he was appointed deputy commander of the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三年，命赴甘肅慶陽督辦糧台，以病請解職回旗。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to go to Qingyang in Gansu to supervise the grain depot; on grounds of illness he requested release from office and return to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to Qingyang in Gansu to supervise the grain depot; citing illness, he requested release from office and return to his banner.

sentences.zh: 七年，起授正藍旗漢軍都統，尋出為福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was recalled and appointed commander of the Han Army Plain Blue Banner; soon he went out as general of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recalled and appointed commander of the Han Army Plain Blue Banner, and soon went out as general of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，兼署閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he concurrently acted as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he concurrently acted as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本兵船窺伺台灣，偕總督​​李鶴年、船政大臣疏陳防務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Japanese warships reconnoitered Taiwan; together with Governor Li Hexian and the minister of the naval administration he memorialized setting forth coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Japanese warships reconnoitered Taiwan; together with Governor Li Hexian and the minister of the naval administration he memorialized on coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，入覲，留京授內大臣、鑲白旗漢軍都統、左都御史，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he came to audience; remaining in the capital he was appointed imperial bodyguard, commander of the Han Army Bordered White Banner, and censor-in-chief of the Left, and was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangxu he came to audience and remained in the capital; he was appointed imperial bodyguard, commander of the Han Army Bordered White Banner, and censor-in-chief of the Left, and was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he became associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 九年，充總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜武英殿大學士，以病乞罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory; on grounds of illness he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, and on grounds of illness requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenda.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督曾國荃等奏文煜咸豐中孤軍捍賊，保全裡下河，請於揚州建專祠，允之。

translations.literal: Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu had fought rebels alone and preserved the Inner Lower River, requesting a dedicated temple be built at Yangzhou; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Zeng Guoquan and others memorialized that in the Xianfeng era Wen Yu had fought rebels alone and preserved the Inner Lower River, and requested a dedicated temple at Yangzhou; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 子志顏，理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhitan was vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhitan was vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 論曰：桂良以帝室葭莩，與聞軍國，數膺議和之使，無所折衝。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Gui Liang, by virtue of kinship with the imperial house, took part in affairs of state and military affairs, and repeatedly received appointments as peace negotiator — yet achieved nothing in struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: Gui Liang, by virtue of kinship with the imperial house, took part in state and military affairs and repeatedly served as peace negotiator — yet achieved nothing in diplomatic standoff.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟從僧格林沁勦賊防夷，曾著勞勚。

translations.literal: Rui Lin followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing rebels and guarding against foreigners, and once won distinguished labor.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing rebels and guarding against foreigners, and once won distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 文煜亦處兵間，無功可錄。

translations.literal: Wen Yu likewise was amid military affairs, with no merit worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yu likewise saw military service, with no merit worth recording.

sentences.zh: 官文雖無過人之才，推賢讓能，奠安江漢，與曾國籓、胡林翼和衷規畫，竟完戡定之功。

translations.literal: Guan Wen, though lacking surpassing talent, recommended the worthy and yielded to the able, settled and secured the Jiang and Han region, and worked in harmonious planning with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi — finally completing the achievement of pacification and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen, though lacking surpassing talent, recommended the worthy and yielded to the able, settled the Jiang and Han region, and worked in harmony with Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi — finally completing the work of pacification.

sentences.zh: 茅土同膺，旂常並煥，豈諸人所可並語哉？

translations.literal: They alike received fiefs and honors; their banners of merit shine together — how can those others be spoken of in the same breath?
translations.idiomatic: They alike received fiefs and honors; their banners of merit shine together — how can those others be spoken of in the same breath?
